task.title: Preserve selected-skill authority across bounded tool steps
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/660 by retaining one exact caller composition through explicit provider/tool continuations without weakening per-invocation authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Validate exact selected skill IDs before provider, authorization, adapter, or durable invocation activity.
Expose caller policies, selected skill blocks, transcript, deterministic tool metadata, and prior tool results as distinct authority or data fields.
Retain the exact initial composition across explicit bounded continuations while each operation calls the provider and dispatches a tool at most once.
Require a fresh invocation identity and authorizer for every tool request, preserve source failures, and leave all existing skill-free APIs behavior-compatible.

attempts.summary: Established RED low-level coverage for composed provider/tool steps.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused runtime test failed because no composed tool request, retained continuation, outcome, or provider traits existed.
attempts.patch: Added coverage for selection rejection, distinct fields, unselected exclusion, final content, retained continuations, fresh authorization and identities, durable evidence, provider failures, and skill-free compatibility.

attempts.summary: Implemented additive bounded composed tool-step orchestration.
attempts.diagnostic: A retained continuation context could preserve immutable caller policy and exact selected blocks while advancing only the exact prior in-memory tool result through the existing durable dispatch boundary.
attempts.patch: Added composed initial and continuation provider contracts, typed requests and outcomes, one-step orchestration, documentation, and the ADR-0005 extension.

attempts.summary: Prevented completed chains from advertising another provider continuation after substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: The first implementation returned Some from continuation() for every completed tool, including ToolStepContinuation::Complete, so Option-driven callers could make one extra provider call.
attempts.patch: Added a regression for completed outcomes, returned a continuation only for ProviderRequired, clarified documentation wording, reran the complete quality gate, and completed exact-head incremental review.

outcome.summary: Provider/tool callers can now advance one explicit bounded step at a time while exact policy and selected-skill authority remain fixed and every requested tool retains fresh caller-owned permission.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30282094141 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/661

lessons: A completion marker must not expose an optional continuation merely because the last bounded step invoked a tool.
Retaining composition inside the outcome prevents callers from substituting policies or selected instructions between provider calls.
Skill authority and tool capability are orthogonal: every tool still needs a fresh identity and one-invocation authorizer.
Explicit one-provider and one-tool bounds make progression caller-owned and prevent a hidden automatic loop.
Incremental review must cover the exact follow-up commit; a rate-limited green status is not review evidence.
